description.narrative:
Youth Voices for Safer Streets is a 12-month youth-led advocacy initiative aimed at strengthening youth representation in policy and community decision-making on substance abuse prevention and road safety in Zambia. The project will build advocacy capacity among young people aged 18–35 years, amplify youth voices in policy dialogues, and promote social norm change around substance use and unsafe road behaviour. Through advocacy training, youth-led policy forums, community dialogues, and development of evidence-based position briefs, the project will enable young people to engage directly with policymakers, enforcement agencies, and community leaders. Implemented by Safe Strides Initiatives, the project leverages existing grassroots networks and institutional partnerships to promote inclusive governance and accountability
Goal: To strengthen youth influence in substance abuse and road safety governance.
Objectives: To build youth advocacy capacity, to increase youth participation in policy dialogue,and to promote safer social norms.
Activities include advocacy training workshops, youth-led policy dialogues, development of youth-informed advocacy briefs, and communityengagement forums.

participating-org.narrative:
Safe Strides Initiatives (SSI) is a youth-led non-governmental organisation founded in October 2024 to address the interconnected challenges of substance abuse and road traffic injuries among adolescents and young people aged 10–35 years in Zambia. Established following an evidence-based needs assessment, SSI responds to key drivers of youth vulnerability, including peer pressure, unemployment, weak enforcement systems, and limited youth-friendly services. The organisation’s vision is to see a generation of empowered youth thriving in safe environments, free from substance abuse and preventable road accidents, and contributing positively to national development. SSI operates through integrated approaches that combine education, peer-led engagement, advocacy, research, and multi-sector partnerships. Its work aligns with Zambia’s Vision 2030 and prioritises community ownership, youth leadership, and evidence-informed programming.
SSI is fully youth-led, with 100% of governance and leadership positions held by young people aged 18–35 years. Youth have primary decision-making authority over strategic direction, programme design, and implementation. More than 80% of operational activities are carried out by trained youth staff and peer educators. Participatory decision-making mechanisms ensure grassroots youth voices directly influence organisational priorities.
